properties.endpoint: The address given to `--http`, or the one a `--serve-shared` daemon announces. A SINGLE MCP endpoint, not a resource tree — every operation is a named tool reached through `tools/call`. `--http-allow-host` restricts which Host headers are accepted; that is a host allowlist, NOT authentication.
properties.error_model: Identical to `ifc:mcp-tools`: JSON-RPC 2.0 `error` responses for transport-level failures, and a normal result carrying `isError: true` with the explanation in the first content block for tool-level ones. A caller that checks only for `error` will read a refused write as a success.
properties.name: MCP tool surface (streamable HTTP transport)
properties.operations: Identical to the stdio transport, because it is the same protocol: `initialize`, the `notifications/initialized` notification, `tools/list`, and `tools/call`. The transport differs; the contract above it does not.
properties.payload_schema: Identical to `ifc:mcp-tools`: `tools/list` returns each tool's `inputSchema` as JSON Schema generated from the Rust request types, so the field-level contract travels with the surface and cannot drift from the build.
properties.spec:
SPLIT OUT OF `ifc:mcp-tools` ON 2026-08-13, ON ANTHONY'S WORD. One Interface had been describing two boundaries — its own `endpoint` said so: *"a stdio pipe to a launched process, OR the address given to `--http`"*. Everything above the transport is identical, because it is the same protocol; what differs is that this one can be reached remotely, can sit behind a gateway, and can terminate TLS, and the stdio one can do none of those.

✅ `medium: json_rpc` SINCE 2026-08-23, ON ANTHONY'S WORD — "add json_rpc and close the stale question". Until then this node carried `unspecified`, and the paragraphs below record why, because the reasoning is what makes the value defensible rather than arbitrary.

WHAT THE BLANK WAS. The enum offered REST / gRPC / event / graphql / cli / library / data / mechanical / electrical / human, and NONE OF THEM NAMED MCP OVER STREAMABLE HTTP. `REST` is wrong: this is not resource-oriented, it is a SINGLE endpoint carrying JSON-RPC 2.0, and every operation is a named tool rather than a verb on a resource. `cli` belongs to the other half. `gRPC` is a different protocol. So `unspecified` was the honest answer to a vocabulary that could not say this — not an oversight, and not a field nobody got round to.

WHY IT WAS ADDED RATHER THAN ENDURED. `medium` is a pairing-key axis and `unspecified` reads as UNKNOWN, never as agreement, so this boundary could pair with NOTHING — including flo2's `ifc:reflow2-design-api`, which is the correspondence a user would actually assert. A permanent blank is not a neutral state; it is a boundary that cannot be checked against anybody.

THE OBJECTION THAT HAD BLOCKED IT, AND HOW IT WAS SETTLED. Adding the value was declined once because enum VALUES are not counted by the version stamp (which counts node and edge TYPES), making a new value a compatibility event nothing can detect — the stamp-blindness pattern this design has recorded four instances of. THE SAME FACT WAS RECORDED TWICE IN THIS PROJECT WITH OPPOSITE CONCLUSIONS: `schema/structure.yaml` cites the stamp's blindness as evidence that adding a value LOCKS NOBODY OUT, i.e. as a reason it is SAFE, while this node cited it as a reason to decline. Settled 2026-08-23 by separating two questions: the missing WORD is fixed, and the stamp not counting vocabulary is a SEPARATE defect with its own history, which is not repaired by leaving a boundary unnameable.

WHAT READS THE NEW VALUE, checked rather than assumed (`dec:edge-orthogonality`: a vocabulary distinction earns its keep only if a computation reads it). Seam pairing compares `medium` as a plain string across `BASE_AXES`, so `json_rpc` matches its like and refuses `REST` with no new branch. `is_foundation_medium` special-cases only `library` and `data` — the media a consumer LINKS AGAINST rather than calls across — and `json_rpc` correctly falls outside it, so the structural detectors go on treating this as a runtime boundary that can fail on its own.

📌 THIS IS THE HALF flo2 ACTUALLY MEANS. Its spec reads *"MCP carried over HTTP, as reflow2 already serves with --http / --serve-shared"*, so the correspondence a user would assert is flo2's `ifc:reflow2-design-api` ↔ THIS node, not the stdio one. The `transport_security` disagreement measured on 2026-08-13 (ours `none`, theirs `tls`) therefore lands here, and lands SHARPER: on a stdio pipe there is no transport to secure and the mismatch could be waved away as a segment artefact, but this boundary really is plain HTTP with no TLS while flo2 says `tls`. **Reading (b) — a real assumption gap — is now the more likely of the two.** STILL OPEN: resolving it needs flo2's side, and setting `medium` does not touch it. What HAS changed is that the two boundaries can now be paired at all, so the disagreement is reachable by a check instead of hidden behind an unknown medium.

✅ `auth: none` and `transport_security: none` are facts: no authentication and no TLS anywhere in `crates/`. `--http-allow-host` is a Host-header allowlist. Terminating TLS and authenticating is `ifc:authenticating-gateway`'s job — a REQUIRED boundary whose name reads "reflow2 has no authentication and is not getting any".
